chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Make up what missed you of the day prayers during the day, and what missed you of the night prayers during the night.' I said: 'Do I make up two Witr prayers in one night?' He said: 'Yes, make up Witr always.'
ai.seo_question: How should missed day and night prayers be made up according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the temporal discipline for qada (making up) prayers, ensuring that the rhythm of worship is maintained by aligning makeup sessions with their original timeframes. The specific instruction to perform Witr as a single unit (not two separate two-rak'ah prayers) reflects the Shia juristic view of Witr as a distinct, singular act of worship rather than merely an extension of the night prayer, preserving its unique status as a sunnah mu'akkadah.
